# Golden fixtures

**Every file here is fictional.** They are generated by a seeded, deterministic generator
(`tools/fixture-gen`). No real trades, accounts, people, brokers' customer data or machine paths are
in them. Tickers are made up (`FIXA` … `FIXF`, `FIX.B`), account numbers are zeros, and every price and
amount is invented. Some files imitate the *layout* of a broker or platform export so the import
code can be tested; their content is still invented.

Don't edit these files by hand. Change the generator and regenerate:

```sh
node tools/fixture-gen/src/cli.ts          # rewrite golden/fixtures/** and manifest.json
node tools/fixture-gen/src/cli.ts --check  # what CI runs: fails if anything differs
```

`manifest.json` lists every fixture with its set, format, kind, the environments it's run in, and its
SHA-256. Line endings, byte-order marks and encodings are part of the data, so `.gitattributes` marks
this folder `-text`.

`<brand>/<fixture>.trades.json` files are the **engine input** for `packages/core`'s parity suite:
`{ "trades": StoredTrade[] }`, the journal the Mac app stored for that fixture (exported from the
Tier B reference by `tools/swift-ref/export-trades.mjs`, one per reference file, so the F7 environment
variants each have one). `F10/` and the `.trades.json` files come from CI, not from the generator,
and the generator leaves them alone.

## Kinds

- **file**: an import file. The Swift harness routes it the way the Mac's Import screen does: by
  file name, then by header detection, then into the column-mapping sheet.
- **journal** (`*-journal.json`): trades exactly as the Mac stores them, including fields that no import
  format carries (tags, emotion, checklist, commission/swap, sector, volume). The harness builds them
  with the app's `Trade` initialiser and stores them through the app's own repository, so storage
  validation applies as it does on the Mac. Values outside the limits (`"NaN"`, `"Infinity"`, `"1e13"`) are
  written as strings on purpose.

## Sets (SPEC §10.3)

| Set | Dojix (forex) | Greenwick (stocks) |
|---|---|---|
| **F1 tiny** | `[100, 50, −30, −20, 80]` in ascending close order. Expectancy 36, maxDD 50, Sharpe 0.6872431934890912, Calmar 3.6. 32-column file and journal | Same profits as a journal and as a NinjaTrader file |
| **F2 year** | 600 trades, 6 pairs, every session, unique close times, no tied group totals. 32-column file plus an annotated journal | 520 trades, 6 tickers (one with a dot, one without a sector), every ET session. Journal and NinjaTrader file |
| **F3 edge cases** | Empty, single, all wins/losses, breakevens, all breakeven, exactly 50% (D-04). JPY pairs and zero SL. Bucket edges (D-01/02/03). 26/27/31/25 columns, quoted and unquoted commas (D-21). LF/CRLF/UTF-8 BOM/UTF-16LE BOM/CP1252. Multi-section file plus a renamed copy. `Trade+Sanitize` limits, nan/inf, control characters, Unicode, invalid rows | Empty, single, all wins/losses, breakevens, 50%. Bucket edges (RVOL, opening range, slippage, duration, R, time-to-MFE). `TradeLimits` rejections. Hostile CSV values. Encodings |
| **F4 long history** | 420 trades: decaying edge, volatility-regime shift, losing late hours (EdgeDecay, KillZone, WhatToCut) | 400 trades with a decaying edge |
| **F5 formats** | MT4 (ticket-0 content tickets, a balance row), cTrader (both header styles, D-15), TradingView (D-16), OANDA, Interactive Brokers, thinkorswim, NinjaTrader, an unknown header, DojixExport (desktop format), an MT5 History report (UTF-16LE HTML, desktop format), 32-column | Interactive Brokers, thinkorswim, TradingView (D-16), NinjaTrader, Webull with and without P&L, an unknown header, Robinhood, Schwab, Fidelity, E*Trade, Tastytrade |
| **F6 FIFO** | — | Every transaction format: 1→n, n→1, shorts, partial fills, same-day sell→buy (D-26), same-timestamp fills, fractional shares, unmatched sells. Option rows (D-22). Schwab without a footer and with the header on line 0 (D-23). Fidelity without a price column (D-24). Robinhood with fees (D-27). Costs on every leg |
| **F7 time** | Midnight-UTC trades in the US (2026-03-08, 2026-11-01) and EU (2026-03-29, 2026-10-25) switch weeks, plus weekend opens. Run in UTC, Europe/Berlin, America/New_York, Asia/Kolkata and Asia/Tokyo with different locales (week starts) | ET trading-day, session and DST boundaries, and Friday-evening closes. Run in the same five environments |
| **F8 tie traps** | Equal group totals. Swift's order is undefined, so these test only the desktop's tie-break and are never compared | Same |
| **F9 scale** | 10k, 50k and 100k trades. Generated on demand (`--scale <dir>`), not committed; their SHA-256 is in the manifest | Same (NinjaTrader files) |
| **F10 Mac backups** | `dojix/F10/`, written by the Mac app's own backup code (Swift harness, CI) from F1: plain SQLite, `DJXB`, `DOJX` | `greenwick/F10/`: plain, `GWBK`, `SJNL` |

Password of the F10 backups: `fixture-password-1` (fictional, test-only). Tampered-header,
wrong-password and too-many-rounds cases are derived from these files in the desktop tests.
